archetype.name: Alpha X (intermediate-volume)
archetype.definition: Tampa's WR1, who soaks up a big share of the team's air yards on routes 10-plus yards downfield and is only as efficient as the quarterback delivering those throws.

report.headline: Separation is up, efficiency is down, and the quarterback room explains most of it.
report.take:
Egbuka's rookie year established his job: 127 targets (9th among receivers), a 34.9% air-yards share (9th) and a 12.2 aDOT. He was the Bucs' downfield chain-mover, with the catch rate that role brings (49.6%, 80th of 86). Four games into year two, the role hasn't changed. His intended air yards sit at 12.8 and he still carries 28.9% of the team's air yards. The surface numbers look worse, though: -0.073 EPA per target (64th of 72) and a 19.6% target share, down from 23.5%.

Split the season by depth and by passer and the picture gets clearer. Underneath he has been excellent: 10 targets from 0-9 yards produced a 90% catch rate and +0.707 EPA per play. The damage comes from the 9 intermediate targets, caught at 44.4% for -0.608 EPA, and 3 deep shots that all fell incomplete. Mayfield's 20 targets to him were worth +0.127 EPA each, which is solidly positive. Jalon Daniels' 4 targets in Week 4 cost -1.072 each, enough on their own to drag the season average below zero. That one game (2 catches, 13 yards, -4.3 EPA) accounts for most of the gap.

The encouraging part is the tracking data. His average separation has climbed from 2.6 yards as a rookie (53rd of 82) to 3.23 on a similar depth of route. He had no charted drops in Weeks 1-3 after a 7.1% drop rate last year. Four games is a hint, not proof, but both point toward a receiver who is winning more cleanly. The worry is everything around him. Tampa's pass offense ranks 31st in EPA, the team is 0-4, and Mayfield's dislocated thumb has an estimated return of Oct. 25.

The near term is a Daniels problem rather than an Egbuka problem. His volume should hold, with 25% of team third-down targets and a WR1 snap share. His efficiency will likely stay muted until Mayfield returns. After that, the improved separation should start turning into the efficient intermediate production his air-yards share implies.

strengths.title: Wins cleanly in the short game
strengths.body: On throws inside 10 yards he has caught nearly everything and created positive plays, including his touchdown. That is the part of the tree that travels to any quarterback because it depends on timing and quick separation, not arm strength. Expect it to carry him while Daniels starts.

strengths.title: Separation jump from rookie year
strengths.body: He is averaging over half a yard more separation than as a rookie on a similar intended depth. That points to sharper route running rather than a change in role, and it is the main reason to expect efficiency to bounce back once the passing gets competent. Over a four-game sample it is a promising sign, not yet a settled trait.

strengths.title: Trusted in money downs
strengths.body: He draws a quarter of Tampa's third-down targets and has converted three into first downs. Along with a full-time snap rate, that locks in his volume floor regardless of who is throwing.

concerns.title: Backup quarterback for at least two more weeks
concerns.body: Mayfield is out with a dislocated thumb and has an estimated Oct. 25 return. Daniels' first start turned Egbuka's targets into heavy negative EPA. A WR1 whose value lives at intermediate depth depends on accurate throws into windows, which is exactly what a backup struggles with. This one is situational and temporary, but it defines the next few games.

concerns.title: Intermediate and deep throws not connecting
concerns.body: Twelve targets at 10-plus air yards have produced four catches and no plays of note downfield. Last year's sub-50% catch rate says some of this is the price of his role. Even so, a combined -2.0 EPA from those depths is poor, partly because Tampa's passing game ranks near the bottom of the league. Expect the deep numbers to improve with Mayfield, but the catch rate on these routes will never be high.

concerns.title: Target share slipping from rookie level
concerns.body: Even with Mayfield healthy, his share of the targets has fallen about four points from last season. Two of his four games came in at 15%. On a run-leaning offense (pass rate 2.6 points under expectation) that caps his ceiling until the share climbs back.

trend.note: His receiving EPA has gone from +4.8 in Week 1 to -4.3 in Week 4. The drop tracks the decline of Tampa's passing game and then the switch to Daniels more than any change in how he is playing.

nextGame.headline: Worst short-pass defense in football, but Daniels throws it
nextGame.body:
Dallas ranks last in pass-defense EPA, last in success rate, last in explosive passes allowed and last against short throws, allowing +0.416 EPA per play there. That last split lines up directly with the one area Egbuka has dominated. The Cowboys rarely sack or hit the quarterback (29th and 26th), which should give Daniels time to find a WR1 on quick and in-breaking routes. Deep throws are Dallas's relative strength (13th in deep EPA), so the path to production is volume underneath rather than chunk plays. A 9.5-point spread against an offense ranked 2nd in EPA projects a trailing game script, which pushes Tampa toward passing more than its run-leaning norm.

Availability favors him on the Dallas side. Starting safety Jalen Thompson is on IR, nickel or rotation corner Cobie Durant is expected to miss the game, and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown is out. That thins out coverage at every level of an already broken pass defense. On Tampa's side, the decisive factor is Mayfield's absence: a second Daniels start, now on four days' rest. McMillan's IR stint removes a depth receiver, which only makes Egbuka's targets steadier.

keyMatchups.title: His short game versus Dallas's worst area
keyMatchups.body: Egbuka's best work this year has come inside 10 yards, and Dallas is the worst defense in the league against short passes. Those are also the throws a backup can most easily complete, so this is where his floor comes from Thursday.

keyMatchups.title: Depleted Cowboys secondary
keyMatchups.body: Losing an 81%-snap safety, a 62%-snap corner and a 74%-snap linebacker strips coverage depth from a unit already allowing the league's highest explosive-pass rate. Receivers against Dallas already average 174 yards a game.

keyMatchups.title: Trailing script with Daniels at QB
keyMatchups.body: As a 9.5-point underdog to a top-three passing offense, Tampa should be throwing more than usual. The question is whether Daniels can hit anything past the sticks after a -1.07 EPA-per-target debut to his WR1.

nextGame.watch: How many of his targets come inside 10 yards. If Daniels leans on quick throws to him rather than forcing intermediate windows, he has a real chance at his best game of the year against this defense.

restOfSeason.body:
The season splits into two phases. With Daniels, likely through about Week 7, expect WR1 volume of roughly 6 targets a game with low efficiency, plus spike potential only against soft defenses like Dallas. Once Mayfield returns, his +0.127 EPA per target with Egbuka is the better baseline. The improved separation and clean hands should lift his intermediate catch rate toward last year's level or better. The 90% short catch rate will regress, and the 0-for-3 deep line will too, in the other direction.

The sustainable parts are the role, the third-down trust and the air-yards share. The touchdown rate is too small a sample to read. The target share is the real question: if it stays near 20% instead of last year's 23.5%, he projects as a solid WR2-level producer rather than the volume WR1 his rookie year suggested.
swingFactors: Mayfield's thumb and actual return date
Whether his target share recovers toward 23%
Intermediate catch rate as separation gains stick

bets.reason: Dallas is last in the league against short passes and is missing a starting safety, a corner and a linebacker. A 9.5-point underdog script should push volume to its WR1, whose short targets have been caught 90% of the time. Daniels is the risk that keeps this a lean.

All four Tampa losses have come by one score, including a 3-point loss with Daniels starting. A defense ranked 5th in EPA and 3rd against the run can keep this closer than the spread implies, and Dallas's own defense ranks 31st. The Cowboys' 2nd-ranked offense is a real threat, so this is a slight lean only.

confidence.note: Four games, a quarterback change, and only one game of data with Daniels.
